title: Financial statements and financial transparency package
status_rationale: No financial statements, accountant reports or bookkeeping records were located. Business plan section 15 contains a draft financial model methodology, not actual results.
target_answer: Because an audit is disproportionate at our stage, we offer a financial transparency package under NDA: annual financial statements reviewed by an independent CPA (moving to audited statements once revenue or customer requirements justify the cost), quarterly management accounts, and a quarterly runway attestation signed by the managing member and supported by a bank balance confirmation. Business and personal finances are fully separated. We state plainly whether any statement is audited, reviewed, compiled or internally prepared.
current_practice: Unknown; no evidence located of books, accounting basis or prepared statements.
intended_practice: Engage a bookkeeper and CPA; produce the first reviewed statements after the first full fiscal year of operations.
customer_statement: Echelon is an early-stage company and does not yet have audited or reviewed financial statements. We will provide a financial transparency package under NDA, and will state the level of assurance of every figure we provide.
residual_risks: Reviewed statements give limited assurance; they are not an audit opinion.
A young company's statements say little about future viability.
open_questions: Which fiscal year end will Echelon use, and has a CPA been identified?

challenge.customer_intent: Confidence that the vendor will remain solvent through the contract term.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Vendor fails mid-contract and the customer loses service or data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Audited statements are backward-looking and for a startup show mainly that cash is limited; they do not predict continuity well.
challenge.legally_required: No law requires a private vendor to provide financial statements; banking guidance expects institutions to assess vendor financial condition.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly requested; often a procurement gate for critical vendors.
challenge.historical_convention: Request two or three years of audited statements.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Escrow, customer-controlled export and the no-funds-held design reduce the harm of failure regardless of financial strength.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Contractual runway-threshold notice triggers transition rights.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Quarterly runway attestation with bank confirmation.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Transparency package plus continuity mitigations (FST-003) instead of audited history.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially: bank confirmation is third-party; runway projection is first-party.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain; some procurement policies hard-require audited statements or minimum revenue.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Attestations prove inaccurate; bank confirmation not obtained.
challenge.conventional_cost: Audit fees: medium to high relative to early revenue.
challenge.alternative_cost: CPA review plus quarterly attestation: low to medium.
challenge.alternative_risks: Customers may treat reviewed statements as audited; Echelon must label assurance level.
supporting_arguments: Addresses the real question (continuity) instead of a historical proxy.
opposing_arguments: Policy-driven procurement may reject anything short of audited statements.
First-party runway figures can be optimistic.

title: Funding, runway, concentration and financial notification covenants
status_rationale: Business plan sections 15.05 (cash flow and reserves) and 15.07 (capital needs) are drafts; no actual funding, cash, burn or revenue data was located.
target_answer: We disclose under NDA our funding sources, cash on hand, monthly net burn, runway, committed funding and revenue concentration, and the decision rules we will apply if funding or revenue falls short. We contractually commit to notify customers within 10 business days if runway falls below 12 months, if a funding commitment fails, or if we lose a customer representing more than a stated share of revenue, and such notice triggers the customer's transition rights and an escrow verification. Our pricing is set to cover cost to serve without subsidy, with cost attribution evidence.
intended_practice: Maintain a driver-based financial model (BP 15.01) updated with actuals monthly; adopt notification covenant in the standard agreement.
customer_statement: Funding and runway information is not yet available in a verifiable form. We are prepared to agree to a contractual notice obligation tied to runway thresholds.
residual_risks: A small company may have very limited runway; notice does not create funding.

title: Insolvency and cessation protection: escrow, wind-down and customer-controlled data
status_rationale: Unbound requirements call for sponsor-controlled exportable data (UNB-CHAR-042), defined vendor exit and recovery responsibility (UNB-GAP-028), a sponsor exit workflow (REQ-X-061) and a design in which Unbound never holds or moves funds (CNV-LEG-001). None is implemented; no escrow agreement or wind-down plan exists.
target_answer: A vendor failure cannot trap customer data or money. Unbound never holds, controls or executes movement of donor or grant funds (CNV-LEG-001). Customers can export their complete records at any time in a documented open format without Echelon involvement, verified by a per-release round-trip test. Source code, build scripts, infrastructure definitions and runbooks for the customer's deployment are deposited with an independent escrow agent at every release, with release conditions including insolvency, cessation of business, failure to support and assignment for benefit of creditors, and the agent performs a build verification at least annually. The license survives bankruptcy and grants the customer a right to host and maintain the software for its own use. A written wind-down plan and a reserve sized to fund an orderly transition period are maintained and tested.
intended_practice: Select an escrow agent; implement export tooling with a release gate; write wind-down plan before first production customer.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to offer verified source and deployment escrow, customer-controlled data export and a funded wind-down plan. These are not yet in place. The Unbound design does not hold or move customer funds.
residual_risks: A customer still needs an operator able to run the escrowed software.
Bankruptcy courts may limit some contractual protections.
open_questions: Which escrow agent and which verification level (deposit, build, full deployment) will Echelon offer?

challenge.customer_intent: Keep operating and keep the data if the vendor fails.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Customer is locked out of records or loses the ability to process grants after vendor insolvency.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Traditional source-only escrow is frequently never verified and often cannot be built when released.
challenge.legally_required: Not required by law; supervisory guidance expects contingency and exit planning for critical third parties.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in bank and enterprise contracts for critical software.
challenge.historical_convention: Source code deposit with a third-party escrow agent, rarely tested.
challenge.architectural_elimination: No-funds-held design removes stranded-funds risk; customer-controlled export removes data lock-in.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release gate fails when export round-trip or escrow deposit job fails.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release deposit receipts and export test results; annual agent verification report.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Verified build-and-deploy escrow plus continuous export, not source-only escrow.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, independently by the escrow agent and directly by the customer.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely for DAF sponsors and smaller institutions; banks may still require vendor financial strength.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Deposits not current; dependencies (including PolyForm-licensed Echelon components) not covered by the escrow license.
challenge.alternative_cost: Verified escrow and export tooling: medium, order-of-magnitude judgment, not sourced.
challenge.alternative_risks: Escrowed code exposes IP to the agent; export of sensitive data must itself be secured.
supporting_arguments: Directly addresses the consequence of vendor failure.
opposing_arguments: Customers rarely have the capacity to operate escrowed software.
Escrow does not help if the cloud account is suspended for non-payment before release.

title: Vendor internal financial controls, banking authority and tax standing
status_rationale: Authorized bank signers and debt approval thresholds are TODO in the formation values file. No accounting controls were located.
target_answer: Company bank accounts require dual authorization above a stated threshold using the bank's own approval workflow, with a second authorized person or an outside accountant; bank statements are reconciled monthly by someone other than the payment initiator, or reviewed by an outside accountant where staff is insufficient. Federal, state and payroll tax filings are current, with no liens. Customer billing is computed from the versioned fee schedule (UNB-SMP-ECN-004) with an auditable calculation trail.
intended_practice: Open business accounts with dual control; engage outside accountant for monthly review.
customer_statement: Internal financial controls are not yet established. We plan dual authorization and outside accountant review of company finances.

title: External financial signals and ongoing financial monitoring
status_rationale: No credit file, D-U-N-S number, bank or trade references were located. Capacity model (BP 15.04) is draft.
target_answer: We authorize customers to obtain a business credit report and provide bank and trade references on request. During the term we notify customers of defined financial events: loss of funding, default on material debt, material litigation, loss of a major customer, and change of control. Our capacity model states how many sponsors of a given size we can onboard and support concurrently, and we decline commitments beyond it.
intended_practice: Establish a business credit file and references once operating; publish capacity limits in onboarding terms.
customer_statement: Business credit and reference information is not yet available. We will agree to notify customers of defined financial events.
